primer_markdown:
## What The Business Is

Netflix, Inc. is a global entertainment company in Communication Services / Entertainment. It operates one of the world’s leading entertainment services, offering TV series, films, games and live programming across genres and languages, with member plans that can be changed over time. ([ir.netflix.net](https://ir.netflix.net/investor-news-and-events/financial-releases/press-release-details/2026/Netflix-to-Announce-First-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx)) The company’s core economic model is paid membership monetization, increasingly supplemented by advertising, pricing/plan optimization, live events, games, podcasts, licensing, and consumer-product extensions.

## What It Does

Netflix acquires, produces, licenses, localizes and distributes entertainment directly to consumers through its streaming platform. Management frames the strategy around: adding more entertainment value; using technology and AI to improve discovery, delivery and production; and improving monetization through pricing, distribution partnerships and a growing ad business. ([s22.q4cdn.com](https://s22.q4cdn.com/959853165/files/doc_financials/2026/q1/FINAL-Q1-26-Shareholder-Letter.pdf)) In Q1 2026, Netflix highlighted expansion beyond traditional series/films into video podcasts, regional live events, a standalone kids gaming app, vertical video on mobile, and GenAI tools via the InterPositive acquisition. ([s22.q4cdn.com](https://s22.q4cdn.com/959853165/files/doc_financials/2026/q1/FINAL-Q1-26-Shareholder-Letter.pdf))

## Recent Highlights (Positive)

- **Q1 execution was ahead of plan.** Netflix reported Q1 2026 revenue of $12.25B, up 16% year over year, with operating income of $3.96B and a 32.3% operating margin; management said revenue and operating income were ahead of guidance due to slightly higher-than-planned subscription revenue. ([s22.q4cdn.com](https://s22.q4cdn.com/959853165/files/doc_financials/2026/q1/FINAL-Q1-26-Shareholder-Letter.pdf))

- **Full-year guide was maintained at a high-margin profile.** Management reaffirmed 2026 revenue guidance of $50.7B–$51.7B, implying 12%–14% growth, and a 31.5% operating-margin target, supported by membership growth, pricing and an expected rough doubling of ad revenue. ([s22.q4cdn.com](https://s22.q4cdn.com/959853165/files/doc_financials/2026/q1/FINAL-Q1-26-Shareholder-Letter.pdf))

- **Advertising scale is becoming more visible.** At its May 2026 Upfront, Netflix said its ad-supported offering reached more than 250M global monthly active viewers and that more than 80% of ad-plan members watch weekly; it also plans to expand the ads plan to 15 additional countries in 2027. ([about.netflix.com](https://about.netflix.com/en/news/netflix-upfront-2026-get-closer?pubDate=20260514))

- **Live events are adding engagement and inventory.** The Q1 World Baseball Classic in Japan drew 31.4M viewers, became Netflix’s most-watched program ever in Japan, and drove the country’s largest sign-up day; the May Upfront also announced more 2026 NFL inventory, including games from Australia, Thanksgiving Eve, Christmas Day and Week 18. ([s22.q4cdn.com](https://s22.q4cdn.com/959853165/files/doc_financials/2026/q1/FINAL-Q1-26-Shareholder-Letter.pdf)) ([about.netflix.com](https://about.netflix.com/en/news/netflix-upfront-2026-get-closer?pubDate=20260514))

## Recent Highlights (Negative)

- **Q2 outlook and lack of a guide raise disappointed investors.** Reuters reported that Netflix shares fell more than 10% after Q1 results as investors weighed a tepid forecast, Reed Hastings’ planned board exit, and questions about the next growth driver.

## Bull Case
Netflix is executing ahead of plan: Q1 2026 revenue of $12.25B (+16% y/y) at a 32.3% operating margin, with full-year guidance of $50.7B–$51.7B reaffirmed at a 31.5% margin. Ad revenue is expected to roughly double, ad-supported MAVs exceed 250M, and live events (WBC Japan, expanded NFL inventory) are broadening engagement and ad inventory. FCF has scaled rapidly — from ~$7.4B to ~$11.9B TTM in one year (+60%) — as content spend growth lags revenue growth. If FCF conversion keeps improving toward ~28–30% of revenue, forward FCF could exceed $15B, and a growth-premium multiple of 28–30x EV/FCF would imply an EV of $420B+ and a market cap well above $400B.

## Bear Case
The stock fell >10% post-Q1 on a tepid Q2 outlook, Reed Hastings' board exit, and questions about the next growth driver. Revenue growth is decelerating from 16% toward 12–14%, ad-scaling benefits may already be priced in, and live/sports content raises cost intensity. If FCF stalls near ~$12.5B and the market compresses the multiple to ~20x on slowing growth, EV would be ~$250B and market cap ~$248B — well below today's ~$321B.

## Logic
- **Forward FCF:** TTM FCF is $11,894M on $46,890M revenue (~25.4% FCF margin). Guidance implies ~$51.2B midpoint 2026 revenue; a 12-month forward revenue of ~$52B with modest margin expansion (~27% FCF conversion, consistent with the recent trajectory of margin gains and ad-revenue doubling) yields forward FCF ≈ **$14,000M** (+18% vs. TTM).
- **Applied multiple:** Current EV/FCF is ~27.2x (inverse of the 3.68% current FCF/EV yield). Given decelerating growth but durable margin expansion and ad optionality, I apply a slightly compressed **26x** EV/forward-FCF.
- **EV:** 14,000 × 26 = **$364,000M**.
- **EV → market cap bridge:** Packet gap = EV − MC = 323,031.4 − 320,930.7 = $2,100.7M net debt. Forward market cap = 364,000 − 2,101 ≈ **$361,900M**.

- Revenue guide of $50.7B–$51.7B (12–14% growth) reaffirmed with a 31.5% operating margin, and ad revenue expected to roughly double — supporting continued FCF conversion improvement.
- FCF momentum is strong: TTM FCF rose from $7.4B (2025) to $11.9B (2026), +60% y/y, driven by scale and margin expansion.
- Advertising (250M+ MAVs), live sports (NFL, WBC), games and podcasts add new monetization vectors that can sustain a premium multiple (25x+ forward FCF), implying an EV toward $360B–$375B and market cap of ~$360B+.

## Bear Case
- Post-Q1 stock fell >10% on a tepid Q2 outlook, Hastings' board exit, and "next growth driver" uncertainty — multiple compression risk is real.
- FCF growth decelerates as content/live-sports spend (NFL rights, events) ramps; forward FCF could land closer to $13B–$13.5B.
- If the market re-rates to ~19–20x EV/FCF (still premium vs. media peers), EV falls to ~$255B–$270B, implying a market cap of ~$255B–$268B.

- **Forward FCF:** TTM FCF is $11,894M. With ~13% revenue growth guided, ad revenue doubling, and margin targets holding at 31.5%, I assume FCF grows ~22% (slower than last year's 60% given rising sports/content cash spend) → **~$14,500M** forward FCF.

- **EV → Market cap bridge:** Current EV ($323,031M) minus market cap ($320,931M) = $2,101M net-debt gap. Forward market cap = 333,500 − 2,101 ≈ **$331,400M**.

- At 20x on ~$13.5B forward FCF, EV would be ~$270B — meaningful downside from the current $323B EV.

## Bull Case
Netflix continues ~13-14% revenue growth toward ~$51B for 2026 with a 31.5% operating margin. Ad revenue roughly doubling, live-events inventory (NFL, WBC), and pricing power expand FCF conversion. FCF grows ~20% off the $11.9B TTM base to ~$14.3B. Market re-rates toward a premium ~30x EV/FCF given durable growth, lifting EV materially above the current ~$323B.

## Bear Case
Post-Q1 selloff signals investor concern over decelerating growth, Hastings' board exit, and absence of a clear next growth driver. Content spend and GenAI investment pressure FCF; growth flattens. FCF grows only modestly to ~$12.5B and the multiple compresses toward the 3y-average FCF/EV (~2.2%, i.e. ~45x looks stretched)—more realistically a discipline toward ~22-24x EV/FCF, pulling EV below current levels.

## Logic
- TTM FCF base: $11,894M. Guidance implies 12-14% revenue growth and stable ~31.5% margins, supporting continued FCF expansion. I apply ~11% forward FCF growth (midpoint of accelerating-then-normalizing scenarios) → forward FCF ≈ $13,200M.

- Forward EV = $13,200M × 26 ≈ $343,200M.
- EV→MC bridge: current EV − MC gap = 323,031.4 − 320,930.7 = $2,100.7M (net debt-like). Forward MC = 343,200 − 2,100.7 ≈ $341,099M.
